originality.rationale: The closest primary theorem (Molchanov–Nagy, arXiv:2610.26108v1, Theorem 5.2) establishes an asymptotic tangent-cone limit conditional on boundary-null measures; it does not establish a finite uniform cutoff or handle atoms. Its Example 5.11 demonstrates eventual stabilization for one specially chosen square distribution and point, not every polytope and all distributions. The explicit finite facet-slack construction is not implied by convergence alone. Actual mathematical-record searches found no identical or dominating result; historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Some earlier statistical-depth literature may contain the finite plateau in alternate language, and the 2007 directional-depth paper was only accessible as an abstract.

The source's general construction makes the present refinement relatively elementary; assess its substantive value from the all-polytope uniform finite cutoff and atomic robustness, not from novelty of definitions or the limiting formula.

value.rationale: The finite, uniform-in-query cutoff for arbitrary compactly supported laws is a qualitative strengthening of an asymptotic tangent-cone theorem, with a geometrically computable threshold and no density assumptions. It reduces every post-cutoff depth query to finitely many one-dimensional marginal tails, applicable to discrete data and high-dimensional polyhedral data depth. The exact uniform-square three-phase onset shows the cutoff phenomenon is not vacuous or mere renaming of a limit. It supplies a natural finite computational horizon and a polyhedral/smooth contrast even without a general downstream theorem.
